goldenPoints: Tall peaked T waves + wide QRS + absent P waves = hyperkalaemia
Wide fixed split of S2 = atrial septal defect
Pistol-shot sound over femorals + collapsing pulse = severe aortic regurgitation
Bacterial meningitis CSF: neutrophils, low glucose, high protein — start antibiotics immediately
Fatigable ptosis improving with neostigmine = myasthenia gravis
HbA1c ≥6.5% is a diagnostic criterion for diabetes mellitus (ADA)
Most common cause of death in childhood DKA is cerebral oedema
Investigation of choice for pulmonary embolism is CT pulmonary angiography
Asbestos exposure is most strongly linked to mesothelioma
Hypertension + hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis = Conn syndrome (primary aldosteronism)
intro: Medicine carries 33 of the 300 FMGE questions, and the papers keep returning to the same ground: ECG identification, valvular murmurs, CSF interpretation, diabetes and thyroid, and classic named syndromes. These notes compress that recurring ground into fact lines — read them after your PYQs, then test yourself with the flashcards.

subject: Medicine
tagline: ECG patterns, murmurs, CSF values and endocrine one-liners — Medicine is FMGE's biggest single subject at 33 questions

topics.oneLiner: Peaked T + wide QRS + absent P = hyperkalaemia until proved otherwise.
points: Hyperkalaemia ECG sequence: tall peaked T waves → flattened/absent P → widened QRS → sine wave
Absent P waves with irregularly irregular pulse = atrial fibrillation
Complete heart block: P waves and QRS complexes march independently; ventricular rate ~35–40/min
STEMI in II, III, aVF = inferior MI, usually right coronary artery territory
Saw-tooth flutter waves, best in V1 and inferior leads = atrial flutter
Polymorphic VT with twisting QRS around baseline = torsades de pointes; treatment is IV magnesium
Pulseless VT/VF: defibrillate; if rhythm persists after shock, resume CPR and give adrenaline
Bedaquiline (anti-TB drug) prolongs the QT interval
topics.title: ECG Patterns & Arrhythmias
topics.trap: Students confuse atrial flutter (saw-tooth, regular) with AF (no P waves, irregularly irregular) — check regularity first.

topics.oneLiner: Fixed split S2 = ASD; collapsing pulse + pistol-shot femorals = AR.
points: Aortic regurgitation: early diastolic murmur at left 3rd intercostal space, water-hammer (collapsing) pulse
Traube sign in severe AR: pistol-shot sound over the femoral arteries
Recent streptococcal throat infection + water-hammer pulse = acute rheumatic AR
Mitral stenosis: mid-diastolic rumbling murmur with opening snap, loud S1
Graham Steell murmur: early diastolic murmur of pulmonary regurgitation due to pulmonary hypertension
ASD gives a wide, fixed split of S2 — the classic fixed-split question
Aortic stenosis: ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids, slow-rising pulse
Infective endocarditis in IV drug users commonly involves the tricuspid valve; Roth spots seen on fundoscopy
topics.title: Valvular Lesions, Murmurs & Heart Sounds
topics.trap: Graham Steell is pulmonary regurgitation secondary to pulmonary hypertension — not a primary valve lesion.

topics.askedAs: NYHA class, JVP pattern, mortality drugs
topics.oneLiner: Kussmaul present = constriction; pulsus paradoxus = tamponade.
points: NYHA II: comfortable at rest, dyspnoea on ordinary activity = mild limitation
Drugs reducing mortality in HFrEF: beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARNI, mineralocorticoid antagonists, SGLT2 inhibitors
Cardiac tamponade — Beck triad: hypotension, muffled heart sounds, raised JVP
Kussmaul sign (JVP rises on inspiration): constrictive pericarditis and restrictive cardiomyopathy
Tamponade shows prominent x descent; constriction shows prominent rapid x and y descents
Pulsus paradoxus (inspiratory systolic BP fall >10 mmHg) is characteristic of tamponade
S3 gallop indicates a dilated, failing ventricle (volume overload)
topics.title: Heart Failure, Tamponade & Constrictive Pericarditis
topics.trap: Both tamponade and constriction raise the JVP — the differentiators are Kussmaul sign and pulsus paradoxus.

topics.askedAs: first step in STEMI, secondary hypertension clues
topics.oneLiner: STEMI = open the artery (PCI first); young hypertensive + low potassium = think Conn.
points: STEMI at a centre with PCI facility: primary PCI is the treatment of choice
Inferior STEMI (II, III, aVF): suspect right ventricular involvement; nitrates can cause severe hypotension
Conn syndrome (primary aldosteronism): hypertension + hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis; sodium is normal/high-normal
Best screening test for Conn syndrome: plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio
DASH diet excludes high-sodium processed foods; it emphasises fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy
Aortic dissection: tearing chest pain radiating to the back; control heart rate and BP (esmolol first) before surgery referral in type A
Post-MI pericarditis with fever and pleuritic pain weeks later = Dressler syndrome
topics.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome & Hypertension
topics.trap: In dissection, giving a pure vasodilator before beta-blockade worsens shear stress — rate control comes first.

topics.oneLiner: Acidotic COPD exacerbation = NIV; low FEV1/FVC = obstruction.
points: Obstructive pattern: reduced FEV1/FVC ratio with reduced FEV1 — asthma and COPD
Acute severe COPD exacerbation with respiratory acidosis (pH <7.35, raised PaCO2): start non-invasive ventilation
Acute severe asthma: nebulised salbutamol, ipratropium, systemic steroids, IV magnesium if poor response
COPD not controlled on a LABA: add a LAMA (e.g. tiotropium) or inhaled steroid per severity
Raised intracranial pressure after head injury: mannitol is the classic osmotic agent asked
Ventilator hypoventilation with respiratory acidosis: increase minute ventilation (rate or tidal volume)
Restrictive pattern: FVC and FEV1 both fall with a normal or high FEV1/FVC ratio — interstitial lung disease
topics.title: Asthma, COPD & Blood Gas Interpretation
topics.trap: Oxygen in COPD is titrated to target saturations of 88–92%, not 100%.

topics.askedAs: Light criteria, investigation of choice, exposure → disease
topics.oneLiner: Suspected PE → CTPA; asbestos → mesothelioma; silica → TB.
points: Light criteria: effusion is exudative if pleural/serum protein >0.5, pleural/serum LDH >0.6, or pleural LDH >2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH
Heart failure effusion is a transudate; low glucose and very high protein point to TB or malignancy
Investigation of choice for pulmonary embolism: CT pulmonary angiography
Asbestos exposure: mesothelioma is the malignancy most strongly linked; shipyard and construction workers
Silica exposure in sandblasting predisposes to tuberculosis (silicotuberculosis)
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: clubbing, fine end-inspiratory crackles; antifibrotics pirfenidone and nintedanib slow progression
Sudden pleuritic pain and desaturation after central line insertion: suspect iatrogenic pneumothorax
topics.title: Pleural Effusion, Pulmonary Embolism & Occupational Lung Disease
topics.trap: A parapneumonic effusion with frank pus or positive Gram stain is an empyema and needs tube drainage, not antibiotics alone.

topics.oneLiner: Neutrophils + low sugar = bacterial; lymphocytes + very high protein = TB.
points: Bacterial meningitis CSF: neutrophils, very low glucose, high protein, turbid appearance
TB meningitis CSF: lymphocytes, low glucose, very high protein; illness runs over days to weeks
Viral meningitis CSF: lymphocytes, normal glucose, mildly raised protein
Cryptococcal meningitis (HIV): India ink shows encapsulated yeast; treatment is amphotericin B-based induction
Start empirical antibiotics immediately in suspected bacterial meningitis — do not wait for imaging or LP if they delay treatment
Subacute meningitis in a child with low CSF glucose and protein of 300 mg% classically means TB meningitis
topics.title: Meningitis & CSF Interpretation
topics.trap: Partially treated bacterial meningitis can look lymphocytic — the clinical tempo and glucose still guide you.

topics.oneLiner: Fatigable ptosis = myasthenia; ascending areflexic weakness = GBS; forehead involved = LMN facial palsy.
points: Myasthenia gravis: fatigable weakness, ptosis worse by evening, improves with rest and neostigmine; decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Guillain–Barré syndrome: ascending symmetric flaccid weakness with areflexia, 1–4 weeks after an infection
Brown–Séquard (cord hemisection): ipsilateral loss of proprioception/vibration below lesion, contralateral loss of pain/temperature starting 1–2 segments below
Absence seizures in a child (brief staring spells): ethosuximide is first-line when only absence seizures occur
Cerebellar lesion: intention tremor, failed finger–nose and heel–shin tests, ataxia — all ipsilateral
Bell palsy: acute unilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness involving the forehead
Duchenne muscular dystrophy: dystrophin completely absent; Becker has reduced/abnormal dystrophin
Thrombolysis-eligible ischaemic stroke: exclude haemorrhage on CT and give IV thrombolytic within the window
topics.title: Weakness, Seizures & Localising Signs
topics.trap: Forehead sparing means an upper motor neuron (central) facial weakness — Bell palsy involves the whole face.

topics.askedAs: ADA criteria, DKA cause of death, syndrome rashes
topics.oneLiner: HbA1c 6.5% diagnoses diabetes; in DKA, watch potassium and the child's brain.
points: ADA diagnosis (any one, confirmed): HbA1c ≥6.5%, fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL, 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL, or random ≥200 mg/dL with classic symptoms
DKA triad: hyperglycaemia, ketosis, metabolic acidosis with Kussmaul breathing and fruity breath
Most common cause of death in DKA in children: cerebral oedema; in adults, hypokalaemia and precipitating illness dominate
In DKA, total body potassium is depleted even when serum potassium looks normal or high
Necrolytic migratory erythema + diabetes + weight loss = glucagonoma
Watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia and achlorhydria (WDHA) = VIPoma (Verner–Morrison syndrome)
Recurrent watery diarrhoea with flushing and right-sided heart disease = carcinoid syndrome
topics.title: Diabetes Mellitus & DKA
topics.trap: Serum potassium in DKA misleads — acidosis shifts potassium out of cells while total body stores are empty.

topics.oneLiner: Paroxysms + metanephrines = phaeochromocytoma; absent bright spot + dilute urine = central DI.
points: Primary hypothyroidism: high TSH with low T3/T4, delayed relaxation of reflexes (slow ankle jerk), cold intolerance
Most common cause of Cushing syndrome overall: exogenous steroid use; of endogenous, pituitary ACTH adenoma (Cushing disease)
Phaeochromocytoma: episodic headache, palpitations, sweating, labile hypertension; screen with plasma/urinary metanephrines
Alpha-blockade must precede beta-blockade in phaeochromocytoma
Central diabetes insipidus: huge urine output, low urine osmolality, low ADH, absent posterior pituitary bright spot on MRI
Diabetes insipidus vs psychogenic polydipsia: DI urine stays dilute despite water deprivation until desmopressin (central) is given
DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion): hypocalcaemia from parathyroid hypoplasia, thymic hypoplasia, conotruncal cardiac defects
Zollinger–Ellison syndrome: gastrinoma with recurrent ulcers; high-dose PPI is the mainstay of acid control
topics.title: Thyroid, Adrenal & Pituitary Disorders
topics.trap: Never beta-block a phaeochromocytoma first — unopposed alpha vasoconstriction can precipitate a hypertensive crisis.

topics.askedAs: ABG values → disorder; AKI vs CKD
topics.oneLiner: Vomiting = hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis; shrunken kidneys = CKD.
points: Recurrent vomiting: metabolic alkalosis (raised pH, raised bicarbonate, compensatory raised PaCO2) with hypokalaemia and hypochloraemia
Hypokalaemia from vomiting/diuretic losses is the classic cause of arrhythmia in severe vomiting
AKI vs CKD: small shrunken kidneys, anaemia, and calcium–phosphate derangement favour CKD; normal kidney size favours AKI
Post-renal obstruction is excluded first with an ultrasound in any unexplained AKI
Nephritic syndrome: haematuria, hypertension, oliguria, mild proteinuria; nephrotic: heavy proteinuria, oedema, hypoalbuminaemia
Acetazolamide acts on the proximal convoluted tubule (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) — used for altitude sickness
High anion gap metabolic acidosis causes: ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, uraemia, salicylates, methanol/ethylene glycol
topics.title: Kidney Disease & Acid–Base Disorders
topics.trap: Compensation never overshoots: a PaCO2 of 48 with bicarbonate 30 and pH 7.5 is primary metabolic alkalosis, not respiratory disease.

topics.oneLiner: Villous atrophy + anti-tTG = coeliac; post-ERCP pain = pancreatitis until disproved.
points: Coeliac disease: villous atrophy on duodenal biopsy, anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA and anti-endomysial antibodies positive
Haemochromatosis: HFE gene mutation (chromosome 6); presents with diabetes, bronze skin, arthropathy, abnormal LFTs
Acute pancreatitis: severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with raised amylase/lipase; most common causes are gallstones and alcohol
Most common complication of ERCP: acute pancreatitis
Achalasia: dysphagia worse for liquids than solids, bird-beak appearance on barium swallow
Ulcerative colitis: continuous colonic inflammation from the rectum with crypt abscesses; Crohn disease: skip lesions and transmural inflammation
ACE-inhibitor cough: dry persistent cough from bradykinin accumulation — a favourite drug-side-effect stem
topics.title: GI & Liver High-Yield
topics.trap: In achalasia liquids are harder than solids; in mechanical obstruction (stricture/cancer) solids are harder — the papers test exactly this reversal.

topics.oneLiner: Young smoker with finger gangrene and normal sugars = Buerger; malar rash + low counts = SLE.
points: SLE: malar rash, oral ulcers, arthritis, cytopenias; anti-dsDNA is the most specific antibody and tracks activity
Antiphospholipid syndrome travels with SLE: thrombosis and recurrent pregnancy loss
Buerger disease (thromboangiitis obliterans): young male smoker, distal limb gangrene and ulcers with normal glucose and lipids
Sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, non-caseating granulomas; steroids are the main treatment when organs are threatened
Aspirin is the drug asked for migratory polyarthritis/carditis pain in acute rheumatic fever
Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetric small-joint polyarthritis with morning stiffness; anti-CCP is the most specific test
Kartagener syndrome: situs inversus, chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis from primary ciliary dyskinesia
topics.title: Rheumatology, Vasculitis & SLE
topics.trap: Kartagener questions are filed under respiratory stems — the triad is ciliary, not cardiac, in origin.

topics.oneLiner: Confusion + ataxia + eye signs = thiamine; eschar + fever = scrub typhus.
points: Wernicke encephalopathy (thiamine deficiency): confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia — classically in chronic alcohol use
Pellagra (niacin deficiency): dermatitis of sun-exposed areas (Casal necklace), diarrhoea, dementia
Riboflavin deficiency: angular cheilitis, glossitis, stomatitis
Vitamin A deficiency: night blindness and xerophthalmia in a poorly nourished child
Scrub typhus: fever with an eschar after mite exposure
Gaucher disease: glucocerebrosidase enzyme deficiency — the classic enzyme-deficiency stem
Re-exposure to dog bite within 3 months of a complete PEP course: wound care only, no vaccine needed; beyond that, two booster doses
IRIS: TB patient worsens paradoxically after starting ART as immunity recovers
Mesothelioma and asbestosis follow asbestos; silicosis follows silica dust in sandblasting and mining
topics.title: Infections, Vitamins & Classic Syndromes
topics.trap: Give thiamine before glucose in a malnourished alcoholic — glucose alone can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy.
